drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna mention that she was sitting on a bed?
outcomeNote: Answer follows in the next unit

segments.he: כֵּיצַד דַּיָּה שְׁעָתָהּ וְכוּ׳. לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנֵי: ״הָיְתָה יוֹשֶׁבֶת בַּמִּטָּה וַעֲסֻקָה בִּטְהָרוֹת״? לִיתְנֵי: ״הָיְתָה עֲסוּקָה בִּטְהָרוֹת וּפָרְשָׁה וְרָאֲתָה״!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches with regard to a woman who has a fixed menstrual cycle: «Her time is sufficient, how so?» If the woman was sitting in a bed and engaged in handling ritually pure items, and she left the bed and saw blood, she is impure and those items are pure. The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need the mishna «to teach:» If the woman «was sitting in a bed and engaged in» handling «pure items? Let» the mishna «teach» the same ruling without mentioning the bed: If she «was engaged in» handling «pure items and she left and saw» blood. The detail that she was sitting in a bed is apparently superfluous.
